# VPP P1898 · Preface by Edward Aveling (1898)

*Preface by Edward Aveling (1898)*

Original: Karl Marx, Value, Price and Profit, ed. Eleanor Marx Aveling (London 1898), public domain; Marxists Internet Archive transcription (proofed by Brandon Poole, 2009; CC BY-SA)  
English: None needed: the original is in English

| Verse | English original (1865, ed. 1898) | Modern draft | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="P1898.0.1"></a>**P1898.0.1** | Preface by Edward Aveling (1898) |  |  |
| <a id="P1898.1.1"></a>**P1898.1.1** | The circumstances under which this paper was read are narrated at the beginning of the work. |  |  |
| <a id="P1898.1.2"></a>**P1898.1.2** | The paper was never published during the lifetime of Marx. |  |  |
| <a id="P1898.1.3"></a>**P1898.1.3** | It was found amongst his papers after the death of Engels. |  |  |
| <a id="P1898.1.4"></a>**P1898.1.4** | Among many other characteristics of Marx, this paper shows two especially. |  |  |
| <a id="P1898.1.5"></a>**P1898.1.5** | These are his patient willingness to make the meaning of his ideas plain to the humblest student, and the extraordinary clearness of those ideas. |  |  |
| <a id="P1898.1.6"></a>**P1898.1.6** | In a partial sense the present volume is an epitome of the first volume of Capital. |  |  |
| <a id="P1898.1.7"></a>**P1898.1.7** | More than one of us have attempted to analyze and simplify that volume, with not too much success perhaps. |  |  |
| <a id="P1898.1.8"></a>**P1898.1.8** | In fact, a witty friend and commentator has suggested that what is now required is an explanation by Marx of our explanations of him. |  |  |
| <a id="P1898.1.9"></a>**P1898.1.9** | I am often asked what is the best succession of books for the student to acquire the fundamental principles of Socialism. |  |  |
| <a id="P1898.1.10"></a>**P1898.1.10** | The question is a difficult one to answer. |  |  |
| <a id="P1898.1.11"></a>**P1898.1.11** | But, by way of suggestion, one might say, first, Engels' Socialism, Scientific And Utopian, then the present work, the first volume of Capital, and the Student's Marx. |  |  |
| <a id="P1898.1.12"></a>**P1898.1.12** | My small part in the preparation of this work has been reading the manuscript, making a few suggestions as to English forms of expression, dividing the work up into chapters and naming the chapters, and revising the proofs for press. |  |  |
| <a id="P1898.1.13"></a>**P1898.1.13** | All the rest, and by far the most important part, of the work has been done by her whose name appears on the title page. |  |  |
| <a id="P1898.1.14"></a>**P1898.1.14** | The present volume has already been translated into German. |  |  |
| <a id="P1898.2.1"></a>**P1898.2.1** | Edward Aveling. |  |  |
